title: Build a one-file CalRatio ABCD extraction prototype and document readiness
body:
Build a small, runnable prototype that tells us whether the inputs for the proposed Run 3 CalRatio ABCD analysis can actually be retrieved. Work from the current specification, use real ATLAS data for the extraction evidence, and finish with a short write-up after two working days. Then pause with a reproducible handoff.

The first physics question is whether we can obtain the two ABCD inputs with the required definitions, from samples that retain the control regions:

- `h = log10(E_H / E_EM)`, including the energy components and their validity.
- The number of qualifying tracks within the specified jet cone, including enough information to establish the track selection.

A generic stored track count or accessible jet-energy accessor must be checked against the specification before being used as the nominal quantity.

1. Read `spec/calratio-abcd-spec.md` and make a compact requirements table for this prototype. Connect each field to its analysis use, units, cardinality, proposed source/accessor, and unresolved physics choices. Include the information needed to assign tag/probe and assess common preselection. Keep the Run 3 trigger, track-definition, and calibration questions explicit.

2. Start from the existing `analysis-data-sources` and `find-atlas-datasets` workflows. Inspect existing probes before creating another extraction skill. Record the specification hash and exact skill/code versions. The older frozen dataset-discovery fixtures are historical evidence; reconcile them with the current specification before reuse.

3. Establish a positive control on the exact Run 3 collision PHYSLITE DID in `spec/calratio-probe-samples.yaml`. Process one file through ServiceX, initially without event or object cuts, retrieving event identity and aligned jet kinematics. Inspect the actual delivered ROOT data for nonzero events, types, units, finite values, and collection alignment. The supplied sample tests extraction; its CalRatio trigger acceptance and analysis suitability still need evidence.

4. Add isolated one-file probes for the calorimeter-energy components, validity information, and track properties needed for the ABCD axes. Distinguish query/API errors, authentication or service failures, demonstrated missing content, and unresolved physics equivalence. Investigate PHYS or a specialist tier when an evidenced PHYSLITE gap warrants it. Document any cross-tier join requirements and checks.

5. Assess candidate samples for the nominal and independent control roles. Check trigger coverage, derivation skims, retained fields, and production provenance. Preserve low-h and nonzero-track populations through extraction. A sample whose upstream selection removed a control region cannot establish ABCD feasibility.

6. Where the inputs permit, produce a small real-data diagnostic with reproducible event selection and tag/probe assignment. Keep region A blinded as required by the specification. Where a required input or physics definition remains unresolved, retain a runnable probe and a precise blocker instead of substituting an unvalidated proxy. Treat any proposed proxy as a separate exploratory option.

Start a new branch from updated `main` and read [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/gordonwatts/iris-hep-llm-performance/blob/main/AGENTS.md) before running work. Preserve unrelated local changes. Resolve the bulk-data root from an explicit task-specific override, then `IRIS_HEP_DATA_DIR`, then `[data].root` in the ignored `data.local.toml`. Each computer supplies its own data location; if none is configured, establish one before downloading large inputs.

Put runnable scripts and instructions under `prototypes/calratio/`. Store downloaded inputs, ROOT ntuples, ServiceX deliveries, full logs/reports, and large exploratory outputs under `<data-root>/calratio/<run-id>/`. Record artifact locations and provenance in small manifests. Keep environments, builds, and latency-sensitive scratch work on a faster disk when available. Keep the PR focused on source, a compact evidence table, selected small diagnostics, and a short status note under `spec/`. Reusable skill improvements belong in `gordonwatts/atlas-analysisbase-marketplace` and should be linked from the PR.

Completion criteria:

- [ ] A documented command runs the one-file extraction attempt with local configuration supplied separately; successful deliveries can be replayed locally. Blocked attempts retain reproducible diagnostics.
- [ ] Evidence records exact queries, DID/file provenance, request identifiers, software versions, observed types/units/counts, and concise failures. Retained or shared artifacts contain no credentials or signed URLs.
- [ ] Every field in the bounded requirements table has inspected extraction evidence or an explicit blocker and next action.
- [ ] Sample identity, field availability, and physics/trigger suitability are reported separately.
- [ ] The PR contains a short status note, preferably no more than 3–5 pages, explaining demonstrated capabilities, unresolved assumptions, and the next decisions requiring physics review.
- [ ] After two working days, freeze the code/input versions, record unfinished work, and pause. An access failure should still leave useful diagnostics and a reviewable status note.

Related work:

- #6 already merged the specification-to-source mapping benchmark.
- #7 and gordonwatts/atlas-analysisbase-marketplace#9 have both merged the newer dataset-manifest workflow. No additional PR merges are prerequisites for starting this issue.
- iris-hep/marketplace#6 tracks reusable analysis techniques. This prototype should provide concrete evidence for later technique work.
